paper.title: Revisiting Sharpness-Aware Minimization: A More Faithful and Effective Implementation

read: full text (arXiv HTML): Sections 1-3, 5-6 and Appendices C (overhead), E (other SAM variants, multi-step, corruptions, alpha dynamics, flatness), F (gradient scale); A (loss-surface visualisations) and B (proofs) skimmed

claims.claim: Sharpness-aware minimization works because the gradient taken at its one-step ascent point, when applied at the current parameters, points closer to the direction of the highest loss in the surrounding neighbourhood than the ordinary gradient does; that approximation is rough, and it gets worse, not better, when the ascent is split into several steps. Supported only if, on loss-surface slices through real training (ResNet-18 / CIFAR-100) and under a second-order approximation, the ascent-point gradient is closer to the direction of the neighbourhood maximum than the local gradient; if plain SAM's test accuracy does not improve, and falls, as the number of ascent steps grows at a fixed total radius; and if multi-step SAM degrades further as the radius grows, while variants that also use earlier ascent gradients do not.
claims.decision_rule: Visualisations and Proposition 1 show g1@theta0 closer to max direction than g0; SAM acc k=1 >= k=2 >= k=4 (CIFAR-100 ResNet-18); SAM k=3 acc decreases with rho while LSAM/MSAM stay flat or rise.

claims.claim: Replacing SAM's update direction with an explicit search for the highest-loss direction at a fixed radius, restricted to the plane spanned by the ascent displacement and the final ascent gradient and refreshed only once per epoch, generalises better than SAM and its multi-step variants at almost no extra cost. Supported only if, with SAM's tuned learning rate, weight decay and radius reused, it beats SAM in test accuracy on all nine combinations of VGG-11, ResNet-18 and DenseNet-121 with CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet, and on ImageNet ResNet-50, IWSLT14 translation and ViT-Ti; if in the multi-step setting it beats every multi-step SAM variant at 1, 2 and 4 steps without losing accuracy as steps increase; if a fixed, grid-searched interpolation direction does worse than the dynamic one; and if training time rises by at most about 5%.
claims.decision_rule: XSAM > SAM on 9/9 single-step settings plus ImageNet, IWSLT14, ViT-Ti; XSAM > SAM, LSAM(+), MSAM(+) at k = 1, 2, 4; XSAM > fixed-alpha WSAM; time overhead <= ~5%.

experiments.text: Define SAM and the explicit variant. Setup: SAM takes k normalised ascent steps of radius rho_i from theta0 and applies the final gradient g_k at theta0. The proposed method spans a plane by v0 (unit vector from theta0 to the final ascent point) and v1 (unit g_k), spherically interpolates v(alpha) between them, picks alpha* maximising the mini-batch loss at theta0 + rho_m v(alpha) over 20-40 values of alpha in [0, 2] or [0, 4], and updates along -v(alpha*) scaled by ||g_k||; alpha* is recomputed at the first iteration of each epoch (over 400 iterations per epoch) and held fixed otherwise. For k = 1 the plane is spanned by g0 and g1.

Visualise and analyse the SAM direction. Setup: loss surfaces on the plane of g0 and g1 at points during ResNet-18 / CIFAR-100 training (e.g. first iteration of epoch 150); a 2D test function with a sharp and a flat minimum for multi-step ascent; a second-order Taylor analysis (Proposition 1). Result: applied at theta0, g1 points closer to the high-loss region than g0 and the loss along it is higher, consistently across visualised iterations, but the match is rough and varies during training; on the 2D function g2 applied at theta0 points toward a flat region, worse than g1; the proposition confirms g1's advantage over g0 under the quadratic approximation. Shrinking the ascent radius to 0 reduces any multi-step gradient back to g0, so a fixed radius is generally suboptimal.

Measure multi-step SAM against variants. Setup: CIFAR-100, ResNet-18, k = 1, 2, 4 with rho = rho*/k, and k = 3 with rho in {0.04, 0.08, 0.12}; MSAM (sum of ascent gradients), LSAM (sum of normalised gradients) and versions also including g0, all rescaled to ||g_k||. Result: SAM 80.93 / 80.91 / 80.65 for k = 1 / 2 / 4 and 80.79 / 80.75 / 79.72 at the three radii with k = 3; LSAM 81.00 / 81.20 / 81.16 and MSAM 81.04 / 81.12 / 80.93 across radii; including g0 (LSAM+) underperforms SAM (80.61 at k = 1, 80.41 at k = 4).

Compare in the single-step setting. Setup: SAM's learning rate, weight decay and rho tuned for SAM on each dataset and reused; 200 epochs; means and standard deviations over seeds. Result: test accuracy SGD / SAM / proposed on CIFAR-10 93.19 / 93.83 / 94.25 (VGG-11), 96.15 / 96.59 / 96.74 (ResNet-18), 96.34 / 96.97 / 97.15 (DenseNet-121); CIFAR-100 71.46 / 74.01 / 74.21, 78.55 / 80.93 / 81.24, 81.78 / 83.81 / 83.96; Tiny-ImageNet 47.44 / 51.96 / 52.58, 57.02 / 62.81 / 63.82, 61.93 / 66.31 / 66.81. Larger tasks, SAM vs proposed: ImageNet ResNet-50 77.04 / 77.22, IWSLT14 BLEU 35.30 / 35.63, ViT-Ti CIFAR-100 67.80 / 68.32. Margins over SAM are 0.15-1.01 points, often within about two standard deviations.

Separate dynamic search from simply mixing directions. Setup: a WSAM-like baseline with a fixed interpolation factor grid-searched over [-1, 3] in steps of 0.25, across radii (single-step and k = 3); multi-step comparison as in the SAM experiment; ASAM, VaSSO and WSAM tuned on CIFAR-100. Result: the fixed factor improves on SAM but the dynamic search is better across radii; multi-step accuracy 81.27 / 81.44 / 81.37 at k = 1 / 2 / 4 against at best 80.93 / 81.18 / 81.01; across radii with k = 3, 81.23 / 81.36 / 81.29. On DenseNet-121 / CIFAR-100, ASAM (83.99) edges out the proposed method (83.96), while combining the two gives 84.06 (81.68 on ResNet-18).

Check cost, stability and flatness. Setup: training time for 200 epochs; alpha* trajectories; update frequency and rho_m sweeps; Hessian eigenvalues by Lanczos and loss-landscape plots on ResNet-18 / CIFAR-10; CIFAR-10-C and CIFAR-100-C. Result: time 0.93 vs 0.96 h (VGG-11 CIFAR-10) up to 16.50 vs 16.55 h (DenseNet-121 Tiny-ImageNet), at most 5% more; alpha* has a clear optimum at each search and drifts smoothly downward; accuracy shows no consistent pattern with update frequency and beats SAM for rho_m from rho to 3 rho; top eigenvalue 33.92 vs 36.15 (SAM) and 78.79 (SGD), lambda1/lambda5 1.59 vs 1.89 and 2.26; corrupted-data accuracy higher overall in all four settings (e.g. 56.37 vs 55.62) but lower than SAM on some categories (noise 25.44 vs 25.58, digital 85.99 vs 86.48).

Note what tuning favours. Setup: all methods reuse SAM's tuned hyperparameters with gradients rescaled to ||g_k||, while the proposed method adds its own neighbourhood radius rho_m (fixed at 0.3 in the radius sweep) and alpha range; the alpha search uses only the current mini-batch. Gains over SAM are a few tenths of a point on CIFAR and ImageNet, so seed variation (standard deviations 0.02-0.42) is comparable to many margins.
